the diffusion behavior of moisture in the underfill is Fickian in nature, and the hygroscopic swelling of underfill is significant comparing with its thermal expansion, and it is temperature dependent.
moisture diffusion in the underfill can be well described with Fick's second law at 60% RH or below, and that hygroscopic expansion is significant and temperature dependent.
the diffusion behavior of an underfills material can be well described using Fick's diffusion law at 60% RH, but non-Fickian behavior occurs at 85% RH.

in-situ characterization of the moisture diffusion and hygroscopic deformation of an underfill epoxy material.
the moisture diffusion behavior, the hygroscopic swelling and the hygrothermal ageing effect of an underfill under different environmental conditions.

moisture diffusion, hygroscopic swelling and the hygrothermal ageing of an epoxy based underfill material, and the results provide important insights to the moisture diffusion and hygroscopic expansion of underfill material in electronic packaging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the moisture absorption-desorption behavior of underfill materials is a complex process, and the moisture diffusion behavior, the moisture-induced swelling behavior, and the damage in the material are all coupled together.

the moisture diffusion and hygroscopic deformation of the underfill material can be described by Fickian diffusion law and linear swelling strain, respectively, when RH is 60% and T < Tg, and non-Fickian and non-linear swelling behaviors occur when the material is exposed at 85%RH and/or T > Tg.

moisture absorption and hygrothermal ageing damage in the underfills are detrimental to the reliability of flip-chip packages, and hygrothermal aging damage in the underfilled joints may cause a significant increase in the coefficient of hygrothermal swelling and the hygroscopic swelling induced strain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hygrothermal ageing effect should be considered for moisture absorption and swelling characterization, especially for the underfill material used in the microelectronic packaging.
the sorption TMA and DMA-RH are powerful in-situ characterization techniques for the study of moisture absorption and hygrothermal ageing effects in polymer composites.

the in-situ sorption TGA is a useful method to measure the moisture diffusivity of underfill material at different RH and temperatures, and the in-situ DMA-Rh is useful to measure the hygroscopic swelling of underfill material.

in-situ DMA-RHG can be used to characterize hygroscopic swelling of the underfill material and it can provide valuable information for the design and optimization of the underfill system.
